title: The Wonderful World of Science — 40-Minute Lesson Plan
subject: Science
objectives: Describe what science is and recognise everyday activities that involve science.
Name the broad branches of science and what each one studies.
List the steps of the scientific method in order.
Apply observation and questioning to a familiar phenomenon.
prerequisites: Students should be comfortable with basic Class 5 science vocabulary.
Familiar with the idea of asking and answering questions.
materials: A clear glass of water and a handful of sugar (for a small demo)
A pencil, a magnet, and an iron nail (for an attention hook)
Notebook and pen for each student
Optional: a printed mind map of the chapter

activities.description: Hook the class with a quick demo. Hold a magnet near an iron nail and ask, 'Why does the nail jump to the magnet without touching?' Take 2-3 student answers without correcting. End with: 'Today we'll learn how science answers questions like this.'
teacher_actions: Pose the question and listen to answers
student_actions: Try to explain in their own words

activities.description: Pair-share activity: each pair lists one thing they noticed on the way to school. Then the teacher prompts them to ask a 'why' or 'how' question about it. A few volunteers share. This shows students they already do science in daily life.
teacher_actions: Pick varied examples to share with the class

activities.description: Mini-lecture: define science as a way of learning by observation, questioning, and testing. Introduce four main branches — physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy — with one familiar example each. Then introduce the scientific method as: observe → ask → hypothesise → test → record → conclude → share.
teacher_actions: Write the definition on the board
Add the branches with a one-line example for each
student_actions: Match each branch with another example from their life

activities.description: Quick demo: dissolve a spoon of sugar in water. Use this to walk through the scientific method live. 'I observed that sugar disappears in water. Question: Where does it go? Hypothesis: It mixes invisibly. Test: taste it (safely!) — sweet means sugar is still there.' Have students apply the same steps to a problem they pick (e.g. why ice melts faster in summer).
student_actions: Write the steps for their chosen example

activities.description: Quick check: 4 oral MCQs picked from the chapter's question bank — 1 on definition, 1 on branches, 1 on the steps of the scientific method, 1 on applying observation. Students show fingers (1/2/3/4) for the option they pick.
teacher_actions: Reteach any item with weak responses
student_actions: Show fingers on the count of three

activities.description: Set homework: each student picks ONE thing they observe at home or on the way to school, writes it as 'I noticed X' + one question + one possible hypothesis they can test the next day. They will share three of these tomorrow.
teacher_actions: Write a model example on the board
Tell students it must be their own observation
student_actions: Pick a phenomenon they're curious about

homework: Make one observation at home and write it in scientific-method form (observation + question + hypothesis + plan to test).
Pick three branches of science and find ONE more example of each from your daily life.
assessment_ideas: Use 5 quick MCQs from the chapter bank as a 'do-now' next class.
Ask students to describe a fair test in their own words during pair work.
Collect homework notebooks every week and check for the scientific-method format.
references: NCERT Class 6 Science 'Curiosity', Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science
